outcome_detail: Both suits active as of mid-2026. The November 17, 2025 suit (filed in Bristol County Superior Court, removed to U.S. District Court of Massachusetts on November 26, 2025) drew motions to dismiss from civilian witness defendants in January 2026 and an answer from former trooper Michael Proctor on January 16, 2026 denying the allegations. The June 4, 2026 suit against the Massachusetts State Police and Canton Police Department is in early litigation; disputes over access to Proctor's phone records were reported in July 2026.
criminal_detail: No criminal charges reported against Michael Proctor or Sean Goode arising from the Read investigation. Proctor was fired by the Massachusetts State Police in March 2025 (an internal trial board also cited driving his cruiser after drinking) and the Massachusetts POST Commission revoked his law enforcement certification. Goode resigned from the Canton Police Department on May 29, 2026 amid termination proceedings.
incident_date_approx: 2022-2025 (investigation and prosecution following the January 2022 death of John O'Keefe)
description: Karen Read, who was acquitted in June 2025 of murdering her boyfriend, Boston police officer John O'Keefe, filed civil suits over the investigation and prosecution of her case. A November 2025 suit against investigators, including former Massachusetts State Police trooper Michael Proctor, and civilian witnesses alleges malicious prosecution and a conspiracy to frame her, and was removed to federal court. A second suit, filed June 4, 2026 in Bristol County Superior Court against the Massachusetts State Police and the Canton Police Department, alleges the agencies employed officers with deep biases against women and cites thousands of text messages by Proctor and former Canton officer Sean Goode containing sexist, racist, antisemitic and homophobic remarks, including crude sexualized comments about Read. The defendants deny wrongdoing; Proctor filed an answer in January 2026 denying that he led a corrupt or biased investigation. Both cases remain pending.
inclusion_concern: This is a malicious-prosecution/civil-rights lawsuit, not a sexual assault or sexual harassment suit. Misogyny is a prominent theme — the complaint cites sexist and sexually crude text messages about the plaintiff by investigators — but no sexual assault or workplace sexual harassment claim is central to the litigation. Sexual-harassment-adjacent at most.
